---
title: Swarm
description: A bounded native chart that routes a message to specialists and carries each returned decision inside its invocation.
---

Swarm routes a message to a specialist, carries the specialist's answer into the next iteration, and stops when routing is done or the handoff budget is reached. Each specialist remains an ordinary Runner.

## Pure routing

<CodeFile path="examples/patterns/06-swarm.ts" region="swarm-recipe" title="examples/patterns/06-swarm.ts (region: swarm-recipe)" />

`swarm({ agents, route, maxHandoffs })` uses a synchronous, pure `route({ message })` function. It runs once per routing iteration and returns a specialist id or `undefined`. A known id dispatches to that specialist; `undefined` or an unknown id halts with the current message.

The native chart records the decision, dispatches through its branch decider, and checks the handoff budget after the specialist returns. Keep the route function free of model calls and other effects.

## A native routing strategy

For model-driven routing, pass `swarm({ agents, router, maxHandoffs })`. RoutingStrategy supplies a once-built `step` runner whose result is a RoutingDecision. Its `message` becomes the next specialist's input, or the final answer when no known specialist is selected.

The swarm mounts the step and reads that invocation's returned decision. `route` and `router` are mutually exclusive; providing both or neither is rejected during construction.

[`llmRouter` and `llmSwarm`](/docs/build/llm-router) compile the roster into a prompt and validate the model's decision. The model's reason remains trace evidence.

## Handoff budget

`maxHandoffs` defaults to 10 and accepts finite integers from 1 through 500. The roster requires at least two specialists with unique ids; `done` is reserved for the halt branch.

Reaching the budget returns the last specialist's answer. There is no extra routing call after the final permitted dispatch.

## Identity and concurrency

Specialists and native routers receive the active composition's parent-run binding. Where the enclosing composition carries a caller identity or request context, that context follows its members; a member never reads the identity of the last direct call on its object. Without an admitted caller identity, the composition's run supplies its conversation identity.

Keep tenant and request admission at the host boundary. The parent binding carries the admitted context; it does not authenticate a caller. A message or routing reason is not an identity carrier.

Await an owned run before starting another on that same runner object. Independently executing parent compositions can mount shared child charts with separate invocation state. See [the native run migration](/docs/build/llm-router#connect-a-router-yourself) for the routing API change.

## Choose a composition

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Pick one specialist for the whole turn | Conditional |
| Return to routing between specialist turns | Swarm |
| Run a fixed pipeline | Sequence or Workflow |
| Fan out independent perspectives and merge | Parallel |
